transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it’s the bridges, really. When I’m driving toward Miami and my car gets to one of those long bridges, I suddenly feel like I can’t do it. My chest tightens up, my hands grip the wheel, and I get this strong feeling that I have to get off right away… even though there’s nowhere to get off.
Do you get this same fear in other places where it might be hard to get away?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it the same way anywhere else. It’s mostly when I’m coming up on those long bridges.
Besides bridges, do you ever get that same fear in other places where it would be hard to leave or get help quickly?
I don’t know that I do. I’ve been trying to think about it, but nothing else really comes to mind the way those bridges do.
Have you ever had one of these sudden panic-like episodes when you were not on a bridge?
Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I get nervous about the bridges, but I don’t remember having that same sudden feeling when I wasn’t on one.
Do you avoid driving on bridges because of this fear?

Yes. I’ve started turning things down if I know I’d have to drive over a long bridge. Gallery openings, birdwatching outings, even some visits with my daughter. I’ll go if someone else can drive me, but otherwise I avoid it. It’s embarrassing, because I’ve always been the one to plan things and handle the driving myself.
When you’re on a long bridge, is the scariest part feeling like you can’t escape or get help if something happens?
I’m not sure it’s exactly that. I don’t really think of it as “I can’t get help,” at least not in so many words. It’s more that once I’m on it, I feel stuck until I’m off, and that’s what gets to me.
When you’re on a long bridge, are you mainly afraid that you’ll suddenly panic?

I think so, yes. The moment my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami, my chest tightens and my hands just clamp down on the wheel. It’s like I suddenly feel I have to get off right away, even though there’s nowhere to go.
If someone else were driving and you were just a passenger on a long bridge, would you still feel that same fear?

Yes, I think I would still feel it. Maybe not quite the same as when I’m the one driving, but on those long bridges toward Miami, it seems to hit as soon as we’re on it. My chest tightens and I get that feeling that I need to be off the bridge, even though I know there isn’t anywhere to go.
Do you feel this same fear in tunnels?
I’m not really sure. I don’t go through tunnels often, so I haven’t noticed the same kind of reaction there.
Do you get this same fear on airplanes?
I’m not really sure. I don’t fly much anymore, so I can’t say I’ve noticed the same feeling on airplanes.
Do you ever avoid being in heavy traffic because you worry you’d feel trapped and unable to get out?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I avoid heavy traffic for that reason, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s more just… I don’t like traffic, but I can’t say I worry about being trapped in it.
If you were standing on a long bridge as a pedestrian, would you still feel that same fear?
I think I would, yes. It’s those long bridges that do it to me. The moment I’m on one, my chest tightens and I feel like I have to get off right away, even though there’s nowhere to go.
When you think about going onto a long bridge, are you afraid of the bridge itself?

Not the bridge itself, exactly. I know those bridges have been there for years, and people drive over them every day. It’s more when I think about being over all that open water—the fear feels much bigger than the real danger.
